sector_model: consumer fintech / short-term lender: judged on net income, credit performance (28-day past due, provision, allowance), funding structure, regulatory exposure, SBC and per-share dilution; operating cash flow is not used alone because member receivable originations sit in investing cash flow; equity is distorted by buybacks
thesis: Dave Inc. (Nasdaq: DAVE) is a US neobank whose profit comes mainly from ExtraCash, a no-interest short-term advance (average term about 12 days) funded through bank partners. Q3 2026 revenue 197.7M (+31%); 9M revenue 526.9M vs 390.5M (+35%); Q3 GAAP net income 63.8M, 9M 128.4M vs 129.9M (2025 held a 26.1M tax benefit; 2026 carries a 30.9M tax expense). Monthly transacting members +18% to 3.15M, originations +23% to 2.5B, 28-day past due 2.09% vs 2.15%. Management raised FY2026 guidance (revenue 746-750M, adjusted EBITDA 327-330M, adjusted EPS 17.45-17.65). TTM GAAP net income 194.4M (FY2025 195.9M minus 9M 2025 129.9M plus 9M 2026 128.4M); at the 2026-11-09 close of 282.65 and 12.79M Class A plus Class V shares (cover, 2026-10-26; identical economics) market cap is about 3.62B: 18.6x TTM GAAP, about 20.5x if 2025 and 2026 pre-tax income are taxed at 21% (own approximation), 16.1x the guided adjusted EPS midpoint. Net cash is thin: 315.1M cash and investments less 200M convertible notes and the 75M facility repaid on 2026-10-08 leaves about 40M. The market had priced the stock up 6.8% on 11-04 and then fell 18.1% on 11-05 after the release; the cause is not confirmed by a read source.
counterthesis: Reported operating cash flow (9M 231.8M) is not owner earnings: originations and collections of member receivables are in investing cash flow (-145.6M in 9M 2025, +25.2M in 9M 2026, the swing mostly reflecting Coastal Community Bank holding 158.8M of ExtraCash off Dave's balance sheet since 2026-06-01 while Dave guarantees it). Pro forma cash generation is therefore well below the headline, and Dave bears credit risk on off-balance-sheet balances capped at 325M after the 2026-11-03 amendment. Provision for credit losses rose 40% in 9M to 92.0M, GAAP net income fell 1% in 9M, adjusted EPS fell 1% in Q3 (4.39 vs 4.45), non-GAAP gross margin slid from 72% to 70% sequentially, and management relaxed legacy fee caps (gross monetization about 7.0% in September), which sits next to open government cases. The DOJ (FTC referral) case against Dave and its CEO survived a motion to dismiss; a Military Lending Act class action is on appeal (argument 2026-11-16); Baltimore and Montgomery County (Pennsylvania, filed 2026-09-28) suits are pending; only 10.0M is accrued and no outcome is estimable. Stock compensation is heavy (45.5M in 9M, 22.0M in Q3, mostly performance units) and Q2 2026 net income was only 6.7M. Equity of 273.8M after 211.9M of buybacks makes price to book (13.2x) meaningless. Customer acquisition cost rose 14% to 22 dollars. Competition from Chime, MoneyLion, Earnin and Brigit.
invalidation: An adverse DOJ/FTC judgment or settlement that restricts fees or imposes large monetary relief; a bank partner ending the program; 28-day past due or provision as a share of originations rising materially; revenue growth falling below about 20% with rising member acquisition cost; or buybacks funded by debt while GAAP income stalls.
